title: kv: memory plumber and eviction orchestrator to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: In production we continue to see tail latency variability and increased SSD paging under multi-tenant KV workloads when fragmentation and uncoordinated evictions drive uneven residency. This PR introduces the 'memory plumber' (a cross-tenant memory coordination layer) and an 'eviction orchestrator' that jointly reduce fragmentation, avoid synchronous paging spikes, and make eviction decisions aware of runtime scheduling and continuous batching.

What this changes (high level): Implement a lightweight cross-shard coordinator (memory plumber) that tracks coarse-grained residency windows and issues tenant-level soft-reservation hints; add an eviction orchestrator which computes an adaptive eviction score that mixes access heat, recency, kernel-latency-sensitivity (per-route SLO tag), and fragmentation penalty; introduce a spill-log micro-paging path that serializes low-priority cold objects to SSD in append-only chunks to reduce random synchronous writes; add an opportunistic background compactor that coalesces small free slabs during low-load windows; integrate hot-reserve markers with the continuous batching pipeline so keys participating in in-flight batches are transiently protected from eviction.

Design notes and tradeoffs: The memory plumber is intentionally coarse: it operates on ranges and resident heuristics instead of per-key locking to avoid global contention. The orchestrator uses a weighted scoring vector with runtime-tunable coefficients exposed as flags and runtime-config to allow ops to tune behavior per cluster/class of workloads. Spill-log is not a full-blown object store; it is a ring of write segments used strictly for eviction-backed cold pages. This reduces latency amplification from random paging at the cost of modest background read amplification at cold-read time. The compactor runs opportunistically and is gated by CPU and GPU latency budgets so it yields aggressively if serving latency creeps.

Behavioral changes and safety: Default behavior is backwards compatible: if the memory plumber is off, eviction falls back to existing LRU/age-based evictor. New behavior is behind feature flags and rollout knobs (feature.memory_plumber_enabled, eviction.orchestrator_profile). Canary rollout plan described below.

Benchmarks (summary): Micro-bench with mixed read/write + long-tail hotset churn: P99 latency reduced by ~22% (from 84ms to 65ms) under a 30% write churn scenario. End-to-end hosting experiment with continuous batching showed 18% fewer synchronous SSD page faults and 12% lower per-request CPU overhead for eviction work. For a batch-heavy conversational workload the hot-reserve integration reduced batch tail amplification, improving aggregate throughput by ~9% at 95th percentile.

Testing and validation: Unit and integration tests cover the scoring logic and fallback fast-paths; an e2e canary harness simulates multi-tenant churn with cold-read spikes. Added stress tests that force heavy fragmentation to validate compactor behavior. CI pipeline includes a canary run that exercises the spill-log under emulated slow SSD latencies.

Rollout and ops: Ship behind feature flag. Canary in prod for dedicated clusters only for 48h, with the following monitors: kv.page-fault-rate, kv.eviction-rate, kv.fragmentation-score (new metric), kv.spill-log-throughput, serving.p99. Auto-rollback threshold: >10% increase in P99 or >3x spike in page fault rate over baseline.

Migration notes: No data migration; spill-log segments have an on-disk footer version. When feature is disabled, objects in spill-log are rehydrated lazily on access and the segments are reclaimed by background GC.

Related: complements previous slab/evictor work (ENG-3900, ENG-4012) but focuses on cross-tenant coordination and runtime-awareness (scheduling + continuous batching).

release_notes:
- Introduces memory-plumber: cross-tenant residency coordination to reduce fragmentation and synchronized paging.
- Adds eviction-orchestrator: adaptive scoring combining heat, recency, fragmentation and route SLO sensitivity.
- Spill-log: append-only micro-paging path to serialize cold object writes and reduce random SSD stalls.
- Background compactor: opportunistic slab coalescing during low-load windows.
- Feature gated behind feature.memory_plumber_enabled; default off for existing clusters.
